 Zverev, Alcaraz learn Nitto ATP Finals draw fate
 12 November 2026 
 By Sam Jacot 
 © ATP Tour 
 Share:
 Play to begin Sunday in Turin 
 World No. 1 Alexander Zverev and second seed Carlos Alcaraz learned their Nitto ATP Finals draw fate on Thursday afternoon in Turin.
 Zverev is a two-time champion at the tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018 and 2021. The German is in John McEnroe Group with Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar. Alcaraz headlines Ivan Lendl Group, which also features Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe. 
 Be part of the action this fortnight in Turin and sign up here to ATP Unlocked for exclusive coverage in the Nitto ATP Finals Hub.
 SINGLES 
 John McEnroe Group:  Alexander Zverev (1), Ben Shelton (3), Arthur Fils (6), Rafael Jodar (8).
 Ivan Lendl Group:  Carlos Alcaraz (2), Daniil Medvedev (4), Flavio Cobolli (5), Frances Tiafoe (7).
 Alcaraz is aiming to triumph at the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time. The Spaniard is making his fourth appearance at the event, with his best result a run to the final last year. The 23-year-old arrives in Turin in red-hot form, having lifted trophies in Paris, Vienna and Tokyo following his return from injury at the US Open.
 Medvedev won the title in 2020, while Shelton is making his second appearance at the event. Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and Jodar are all making their debuts. Home favourite Cobolli leads the Italian charge, with Jannik Sinner missing the tournament due to injury.
 The doubles draw was also revealed Thursday. Top seeds Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten are the defending champions and headline Todd Woodbridge Group with Marcelo Arevalo/Mate Pavic, Theo Arribage/Albano Olivetti and Orlando Luz/Rafael Matos. Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski lead Mark Woodforde Group with Marcel Granollers/Horacio Zeballos, Simone Bolelli/Andrea Vavassori and Kevin Krawietz/Tim Puetz.
 DOUBLES
Todd Woodbridge Group:  Harri Heliovaara/Henry Patten (1), Marcelo Arevalo/Mate Pavic (4), Theo Arribage/Albano Olivetti (6), Orlando Luz/Rafael Matos (8).
 Mark Woodforde Group: Christian Harrison/Neal Skupski (2), Marcel Granollers/Horacio Zeballos (3), Simone Bolelli/Andrea Vavassori (5), Kevin Krawietz/Tim Puetz (7).
 The action takes place at Inalpi Arena from 15-22 November.
